text:
maria.garcia: quick follow-up to the adaptive-probe RFC — i sketched a refactor where per-ingress proxies own short-lived quota scoring (100ms budget) and emit compact abuse signals to central scoring. thoughts?
kevin.cho: hmm. local scoring would cut p99 by a lot but how do we keep fairness across regions when proxies make independent admits?
devin: we can attach a cheap global token hint (leaky counter) — not authoritative, just a tie-breaker when local scores are close. keeps common case local.
sara_sre: sounds promising. concern: abuse signals leaving proxies might be noisy. how do we avoid false-positive global blacklisting?
maria.garcia: plan is to use two channels: (1) immediate local verdict for latency-sensitive admits, (2) aggregated signals with windowed decay for central decisions. central only acts on aggregated evidence.
kevin.cho: tradeoff is eventual consistency — a client could game different regions before the aggregator penalizes them. any mitigation?
devin: add short-lived cross-region leases for high-risk clients. if a proxy sees burst + high score it requests a quick lease from central (50ms sync path). fall back to local admit if central times out.
sara_sre: fallback behavior needs to be explicit in SLOs. we can't silently increase error surface. recommend a canary with 1% traffic and telemetry hooks.
maria.garcia: agreed. telemetry: include delta between local-score and global-score, lease latencies, and counts of fallback admits. wire those to the console dashboards.
kevin.cho: on the signal schema: keep it minimal (client_id, short histogram, coarse-abuse-class, ttl). avoid sending full request fingerprints. privacy + perf.
devin: implementation sketch: proxies run a small sliding-window scorer (n=200 samples), maintain `recent_badness` float, emit samples every 5s to aggregator. aggregator keeps decay half-life = 30s.
sara_sre: what about quota accounting correctness for reserved Dedicated capacity? can't let local admits forfeit committed capacity billing.
maria.garcia: for reserved pools we flip: central admission authoritative, proxies only pre-admit and acquire a short token lease from the reserved allocator. for hosted (best-effort) proxies operate in the local-first mode.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging build 2034 pushed with feature toggle `local_scoring_v2` enabled for 1% canary.
kevin.cho: rollout checklist: (1) canary proxy image with toggle, (2) aggregator running in read-only mode initially, (3) alert on score divergence > 0.25 for 5m, (4) SLA playbook updated.
devin: tests: synthetic client that simulates cross-region burst, verify aggregator catches pattern within 90s, and verify fallback lease path latency under 60ms.
sara_sre: also add chaos test where aggregator is partitioned for 2m to ensure safe local behavior.
maria.garcia: i'll draft RFC follow-up with diagrams and the rollout plan. tagging @kevin.cho @devin for review. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
kevin.cho: +1 — please add a short section on audit logs and signal retention (30d) for compliance.
devin: will add retention + example of compact signal envelope.
sara_sre: if you want i can own the canary ops run next week.
maria.garcia: appreciate it. filing the follow-up now: https://go/repo/r/adaptive-probe-refactor (PR incoming)
ops-bot: ci-bot: CI pipeline passed for branch `adaptive-probe-refactor-mg/1`
kevin.cho: ok lets sync after PR, thanks all.
